title: Strong Subadditivity of Shannon Entropy
description: H(X,Y,Z) + H(Y) ≤ H(X,Y) + H(Y,Z): strong subadditivity via conditional mutual information non-negativity

meta.author: Lieb-Ruskai (1973) for quantum, classical follows from KL divergence
originalContributions: Conditional entropy H(X|Y,Z) and conditional mutual information I(X;Z|Y)
Equivalence of strong subadditivity forms (form 1 ↔ form 3, verified)
Framework for proving from KL divergence non-negativity
meta.assumptions: 2 axioms: strong_subadditivity (form 1) and condMutualInfo_nonneg (form 3). Both provable from KL divergence non-negativity (already in ShannonEntropy.lean).

overview.historicalContext: Strong subadditivity was proved by Lieb and Ruskai (1973) for von Neumann (quantum) entropy. The classical case follows more simply from the non-negativity of KL divergence.
overview.problemStatement: Prove H(X,Y,Z) + H(Y) ≤ H(X,Y) + H(Y,Z) from the log-sum inequality.
overview.text: Strong subadditivity of Shannon entropy via conditional mutual information
overview.proofStrategy: I(X;Z|Y) = Σ_y p(y) D_KL(p(x,z|y) || p(x|y)p(z|y)) ≥ 0 since each term is a non-negative KL divergence.
keyInsights: Strong subadditivity = conditioning reduces entropy = conditional MI ≥ 0. Three equivalent forms, all following from KL ≥ 0.

sections.title: Marginal Distributions
sections.mathContext: Summing out variables to get marginal distributions.

sections.title: Strong Subadditivity
sections.summary: Two axiomatized forms plus verified equivalence.

crossReferences.description: Extends ShannonEntropy.lean to three-variable distributions and strong subadditivity.

conclusion.summary: Definitions and framework for strong subadditivity. Equivalence of the three standard forms is verified. The main inequalities are axiomatized, provable from existing KL ≥ 0 infrastructure.
conclusion.implications: Strong subadditivity is the foundation of quantum information theory and data processing inequalities.
openQuestions: Can the axioms be eliminated by applying kl_divergence_nonneg to the conditional distribution?
